properties.note: Fire of 21 September 1776. Source text: 'the fire began in the Fighting Cocks Tavern, near Whitehall Slip ... the flames spread north and west ... The fire crossed Broadway near Beaver Street and then burned most of the city between Broadway and the Hudson River ... It may also have been stopped by the relatively undeveloped property of King's College, located at the northern end of the fire-damaged area ... Estimates for the number of buildings destroyed range from 400 to 1,000 ... Among the buildings destroyed was Trinity Church ...; St. Paul's Chapel survived.' Drawn from that: ring south = Whitehall St to Broad St, Pearl St to Beaver St (ESTIMATED: the text gives only the start and the crossing point); ring west = Broadway to the Hudson shore of 1767 from Beaver St to Barclay St (King's College stood between Barclay and Murray Sts), without the St Paul's block (Broadway - Church St, north of Fulton St). The article reproduces a 1776 map with the burned blocks marked in red ('over 20 city blocks'); it was not traced here. Not a retreat of the built-up area: do not subtract it from the extents, end the buildings inside it in 1776.
properties.method: ESTIMATED outline from a text, not from a map of the burned district
